title: Boosting Entropy with Bell Box Quantization
claim: A heavy-tailed distribution is transformed step by step into a uniform one, then quantized, so every level is used equally.
layout: 4 histogram panels, left-to-right, math formula titles above, step labels below
description: Four blue histograms in a row show how a distribution changes through the BBQ quantizer. The first panel, labeled 'Weights or Activations', is a sharply peaked, heavy-tailed distribution of x centered at 0. Step (a), 'HT & RMS', gives a smooth bell-shaped distribution of v = HT(x)/σ over roughly -3 to 3. Step (b), 'PIT', applies Φ(v) and produces a flat, near-uniform rectangle on [0,1]. Step (c), 'Uniform Quantization', shows 16 evenly spaced thin bars on an axis from -8 to 8, which are the discrete 4-bit levels. Each panel has its formula as a title and its step name as a caption. The figure uses one blue color on white. The eye goes first to the contrast between the spike, the bell, the box and the comb.
caption: The three steps of the BBQ quantization formula (Equation [ref]) for $b=4$. Step \subref{fig:1a} is the Hadamard Transform (HT) followed by RMS Normalization. Step \subref{fig:1b} is the probability integral transform (PIT). Step \subref{fig:1c} is uniform quantization. We name our method Bell Box Quantization because Figure [ref] looks like a bell and Figure [ref] looks like a box (rectangle) which is quantized in Figure [ref].
abstract: Quantization-Aware Pre-Training (QAPT) is an effective technique to reduce the compute and memory overhead of Deep Neural Networks while improving their energy efficiency on edge devices. Existing QAPT methods produce models stored in compute-efficient data types (e.g. integers) that are not information theoretically optimal (ITO). On the other hand, existing ITO data types (e.g. Quantile/NormalFloat Quantization) are not compute-efficient. We propose BBQ, the first ITO quantization method that is also compute-efficient. BBQ builds on our key insight that since learning is domain-agnostic, the output of a quantizer does not need to reside in the same domain as its input. BBQ performs ITO quantization in its input domain, and returns its output in a compute-efficient domain where ITO data types are mapped to compute-efficient data types. Without sacrificing compute efficiency, BBQ outperforms prior SOTA QAPT methods by a perplexity reduction of up to 2 points for 4-bit models, up to 4 points for 3-bit models, up to 5 points for 2-bit models, and up to 18 points for 1-bit models. Code is available at https://github.com/1733116199/bbq.
